title: Sources of finance
examples: What is the difference between internal and external finance?
When should a business use short-term funding?
Can a business use its own profits for expansion?

explain.say: Today we are learning about where businesses get money.

draw.text: Sources of Finance: Internal vs External

explain.say: First we look at internal sources of finance.

items: Retained profit: Money kept in business
Sale of assets: Selling old equipment

explain.say: Next we study external sources of finance.

items: Share capital: Selling shares to investors

explain.say: We now look at short-term finance options.
Finally we examine long-term finance options for growth.
Imagine a local bakery wants to open a second shop.

faq.q: What is the main difference between internal and external finance?
faq.a: Internal finance comes from the business itself, like profits. External finance comes from people or institutions outside the business.
asks: Where does a business get its own money from?

faq.q: When should a business use short-term finance?
faq.a: Short-term finance is best for covering immediate, short-term needs, like buying stock before sales arrive.
asks: What is trade credit used for?

faq.q: Can I use retained profit for everything?
faq.a: No, while retained profit is useful, it should be managed carefully for the right purpose.
asks: Is there a limit to using profits?
Can I use profits to buy new machines?

faq.q: What is the risk of using bank loans?
faq.a: The risk is that you must repay the loan with interest, even if the business is slow.
asks: Do I always have to pay back a loan?
What happens if I cannot repay the bank?

faq.q: Is selling shares always the best option?
faq.a: Selling shares means giving away a part of ownership, which is a big commitment for the business.
asks: What does giving away shares mean?

facts: Internal finance uses money the business has already earned.
External finance involves borrowing or selling ownership to outsiders.
Short-term finance covers needs lasting less than one year.
Long-term finance is used for major, lasting investments.

quiz.say: A business needs cash quickly to buy seasonal stock.
quiz.why: This is a short-term need, and an overdraft is designed for quick cash gaps.

wrong.1: A mortgage is for long-term assets like property, not quick stock purchases.
wrong.2: Retained profit is money already earned, not a facility for immediate borrowing.
wrong.3: Share capital involves giving away ownership, which is too big a step for a quick cash gap.

quiz.say: A company wants to build a new factory over many years.
quiz.why: Building a factory is a major, lasting investment requiring funds over many years.

wrong.1: Trade credit is only for buying goods, not building large structures.
wrong.2: Overdrafts are only suitable for very short-term cash flow issues.
wrong.3: While profits help, large factory builds often require more capital than profits alone.

quiz.say: A business owner uses money from selling old machinery.
quiz.why: Selling old equipment is a direct way to generate internal cash.

wrong.0: An overdraft is borrowing money, not generating it by selling property.
wrong.2: A bank loan requires the business to pay back money to a bank.
wrong.3: Share capital means selling ownership shares, not selling physical items.
